clue.text: Road user growth swelled by 151

indicators.note: something swelled by an addition takes it inside and grows, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: a cyst is an abnormal growth in the body
151 in Roman numerals is CLI

explanation.surface: A note on a road user whose numbers have grown by 151.
explanation.walkthrough: The number is not a cross-reference; it is spelt in Roman numerals as C, L and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclist rides a bicycle on the highway, and so is one of the people who use roads.

clue.text: Senior director holds a minute or very small role

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within your grasp, so the outer piece encloses the other

blocks.note: CEO is a chief executive officer, the senior company director
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: A company boss holds a meeting for a minute or takes only a tiny part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' could be tiny, fitting 'very small', but it is the time unit's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a brief appearance in a film or play, often by a famous person, so it is a tiny part.

clue.text: Found part of Bible set up as a revered item

indicators.note: in a down entry, setting something up raises it so it reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: met means came across, or found
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A section of scripture is found and set up as a sacred object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the verb to establish; it is the past tense of find.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or emblem treated as sacred by a group, so it is something held in reverence.

clue.text: Fur bought initially during offer period

indicators.note: initially means at the very start, so only the opening letter is kept
what happens during a stretch of time falls inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a sale is a period of special offers
the first letter of bought

explanation.surface: A fur coat bought in the first days of a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: The scene is a shopping trip, so 'offer period' seems like padding; it is the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the dark, highly prized pelt of a small marten found in Siberia, so it is a fur.

clue.text: Go beyond one small tango in unfashionable foxtrot?

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so those pieces go within another

blocks.note: out means no longer in fashion
the foxtrot is an example of a dance, signalled by the question mark
the Roman numeral for one
S is the abbreviation for small
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dancer goes too far, slipping a bit of tango into an old-fashioned foxtrot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tango' and 'foxtrot' both look like dances, but only one is; the other is the radio alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdistance rivals is to get further ahead of them, which is to go beyond them in a race.

clue.text: Hillary perhaps organising team reunion

indicators.note: to organise things is to arrange them into order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician named Hillary plans a get-together for an old team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hillary' suggests the American politician; it is Sir Edmund Hillary, who with Tenzing Norgay first climbed Everest in 1953.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Hillary is a famous example of a climber of high peaks, and 'perhaps' signals he is one instance.

clue.text: Believing in an illusion of Christ, refer to fish being turned

definitions.text: Believing in an illusion of Christ

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so the letters read right to left

blocks.note: to cite a source is to refer to it
a cod is a fish

explanation.surface: A believer in a vision of Christ mentions the miracle of the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The fish suits the Gospel setting, but it is just a cod; the obscure word is best reached by reversing the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Docetism was an early heresy holding that Christ's body was only apparent, a phantom, so its followers were docetic.

clue.text: Carbuncle, gemstone in the end certainly something from a mine

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is taken

blocks.note: the last letter of gemstone
yes is said to mean certainly
ore is rock dug from a mine for its metal

explanation.surface: A carbuncle is a red gemstone, and in the end, certainly, it comes from a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: A carbuncle is both a garnet, fitting 'gemstone', and an ugly building, famously Prince Charles's 'monstrous carbuncle'; the second sense is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In British use a carbuncle is an ugly building spoiling its surroundings, which is something unpleasant to look at.

clue.text: Foul fiend featured in sermon’s terrifying

indicators.note: something featured in a piece appears within it, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A preacher describes a dreadful devil in a frightening sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: The fiend fits the hellfire sermon perfectly, which hides that it is spelt out across the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A foul fiend is an evil, frightening creature, and a monster is likewise a horrible and wicked being.
